config.language: Pebble's language: the interface, the texts it writes (path, skeletons, bootstrap) and the model's answers.
config.language.enum0: Follows VS Code's language (Italian if VS Code is in Italian, English otherwise)
config.experienceLevel: Your experience level: it changes what Pebble flags, how it explains it and the shape of the code you ask for.
config.ghost.roadmap.provider: Provider for the Roadmap ghost (plans, adoption, next step, prepared files). Empty: the default provider. Recommended: a strong model.
config.ghost.mentor.provider: Provider for the Mentor ghost (chat, reviews, tests, new files, the help ladder). Empty: the default provider. Recommended: a mid, low-cost model.
config.ghost.assist.provider: Provider for the ⌥P helper ghost (the tabs of the help panel). Empty: the default provider. A cheap or local model is enough.
config.ghost.git.provider: Provider for the Git ghost (explaining a merge or rebase conflict; the repo state and the cards use no model). Empty: the default provider.
config.ghost.model: Model for this ghost. Empty: the default provider's model.
config.ghost.effort: Effort for this ghost (Claude only). Empty: the default effort.
config.training: Training: Pebble doesn't write your project's logic, even if you ask. Questions, directions, pseudocode and examples on different cases, up to the exact line (ADR-016).
config.experienceLevel.enum0: I'm learning to program: simple explanations, terms explained; code you ask for is complete and explained line by line
config.experienceLevel.enum1: I can program but have little project experience: the why, with the principles named; complete code
config.experienceLevel.enum2: I'm autonomous: default behaviour; lean code with the choices motivated
config.experienceLevel.enum3: Expert: only bugs, ADR violations and trade-offs, terse answers; targeted patches
config.provider.enum2: Local model with an OpenAI-compatible API (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp)
config.anthropic.effort: How much Claude reasons: higher = more accurate, slower and more expensive answers.
config.openai.model: OpenAI model to use (required if the provider is OpenAI).
config.local.baseUrl: Address of the local server's OpenAI-compatible API. Ollama: http://localhost:11434/v1 · LM Studio: http://localhost:1234/v1
config.local.model: Local model name (e.g. the one you see with `ollama list`).
config.monthlyBudgetUsd: Monthly budget in dollars. When you go over it, Pebble warns you and the status bar turns yellow. 0 = no budget.
config.prices: Prices for models Pebble doesn't know (e.g. OpenAI), in dollars per million tokens. Example: `{ "gpt-6.2-sol": { "input": 2, "output": 8, "cacheRead": 0.2 } }`. Claude prices are already included.
config.autoStart: When you open a project with bootstrap.md but without .pebble/, Pebble reads it and proposes the plan (once per project).
config.guideNewFiles: When you create a file in a project with .pebble/, Pebble tells you its role and what to avoid.
config.path.testCommand: Command that runs the tests, run in the project folder. Pebble reads TAP and the output of `swift test`, `pytest -v`, `go test -v` and `cargo test`. If you leave the default, Pebble picks one from the manifest: package.json (Vitest included), Package.swift, pyproject.toml/requirements.txt, go.mod, Cargo.toml. Examples: `node --test --test-reporter=tap "test/**/*.test.ts"`, `npx vitest run --reporter=tap-flat`.
config.path.testTimeoutSeconds: Maximum time for the tests run by the path, in seconds.
config.path.verifyOnSave: When you save a project file, rerun the tests and update the path's boxes. It doesn't use the model and costs nothing.
config.path.requireRedFirst: A task closes only if Pebble has seen its tests fail at least once (ADR-010). Off: the task closes with a warning.
description: Walk the path. You write the code. A pair engineer in your editor: it plans the path, prepares the structure, checks your work with your tests and helps you think.
